> Encryption in transit protects data while it moves, using TLS, so anyone intercepting the connection sees scrambled bytes rather than your data; it is what…

Encryption at rest protects data while it is stored, using strong ciphers like AES-256 on disks, databases, backups, and object storage, so a stolen drive or a leaked backup is unreadable. The nuance most people miss: encryption at rest protects the physical media, not your live application. It is transparent to anyone with legitimate access, so it does nothing against a leaked password, a SQL injection, or a compromised app.

> Encryption in transit protects data while it moves, using TLS, so anyone intercepting the connection sees scrambled bytes rather than your data; it is what the browser padlock represents.
Encryption at rest protects data while it is stored, using strong ciphers like AES-256 on disks, databases, backups, and object storage, so a stolen drive or a leaked backup is unreadable.
The nuance most people miss: encryption at rest protects the physical media, not your live application.
It is transparent to anyone with legitimate access, so it does nothing against a leaked password, a SQL injection, or a compromised app.
